    APPLICANTS’ RESPONSE TO ALBERT L. ANDERSON FAMILY LP AND DEANN
         DUNGAN’S OBJECTIONS TO APPLICANTS’ DIRECT TESTIMONY

        Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (“LCRA TSC,” together, “Applicants”) respectfully file this response to the

objections to Applicants’ direct testimony filed by Albert L. Anderson Family Limited Partnership

and DeAnn Dungan (collectively, the “Anderson Intervenors”). 1 Pursuant to 16 Tex. Admin. Code

§ 22.78, this response is timely filed. Applicants respectfully show as follows:

       I.      THE ANDERSON INTERVENORS’ OBJECTIONS ARE UNTIMELY

        SOAH Order No. 6 established a deadline of May 6, 2026, for parties to file objections to

Applicants’ direct testimony. 2 The Anderson Intervenors filed their objections on May 18, 2026,

twelve days past the deadline. The Anderson Intervenors provided no justification for the


1
  Albert L. Anderson Family Limited Partnership and DeAnn Dungan’s Objections to Applicants’ Direct Testimony
(May 18, 2026) (Item No. 4719) (“Anderson Intervenors’ Objections”).
2
  SOAH Order No. 6 – Memorializing Prehearing Conference; Granting Good-Cause Exception; Extending Comment
Deadline on Application & Notice; Adopting Schedule; Setting Route Adequacy & Merits Hearings; Addressing
Procedures; Advising Intervenors on Dismissal (Apr. 20, 2026) (Item No. 788).

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                     1
 untimeliness of their filing. Indeed, the filing failed to provide any basis for which the

Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) could find that good cause exists to allow the objections

nearly two weeks late. Because the Anderson Intervenors have offered no good cause for the late

filing, nor have they sought leave from the ALJs to file objections out of time, the Anderson

Intervenors’ Objections should be overruled.

           II.      THE ANDERSON INTERVENORS’ OBJECTIONS ARE MERITLESS

        Even if the Anderson Intervenors’ Objections were timely, they should be overruled on

substantive grounds because they do not properly challenge the admissibility of Applicants’

testimony. Rather, the Anderson Intervenors merely disagree with the conclusions reached in

Applicants’ direct testimonies and are improperly using thinly-veiled “objections” as a vehicle to

exclude testimony rather than rebut it with their own evidence. These challenges to Applicants’

direct testimonies cite no case law nor evidentiary rules supporting the objections and frequently

fail to state the particular objection that is being asserted. They also mischaracterize Applicants’

testimonies in order to manufacture something to object to and therefore should be read carefully

and skeptically. “Evidentiary objections must be timely, specific, and afford the trial court an

opportunity to cure the alleged error, if any. The Texas Rules of Evidence require the ALJs to rule

on the specific admissibility of individual testimony and exhibit as they are offered, not in

sweeping classifications.” 3 For the following reasons, each objection should be overruled.

A. Objections to the testimony of Russell Marusak




3
 Joint Application of AEP Texas Inc. and City of San Antonio, Acting by and Through the City Public Service Board
(CPS Energy) to Amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity for the Howard to Solstice 765-kV Single-
Circuit Transmission Line in Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, Crockett, Edwards, Kerr, Kinney, Medina, Pecos, Real,
Sutton, Terrell, Uvalde, and Val Verde Counties, Docket No. 59336, SOAH Order No. 11 – Order Ruling on
Objections to Intervenor and Staff Testimony (May 6, 2026) (internal citations omitted).

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                       2
 1. Marusak Direct at 21:11-12

        The Anderson Intervenors object to Mr. Russell Marusak’s testimony that states, “all

alternative routes ‘adhere to the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.’ (Marusak Direct at

21:11-12).” 4 In asserting that the testimony is conclusory, the Anderson Intervenors completely

ignore the discussion in Mr. Marusak’s testimony that supports his conclusion. Specifically, Mr.

Marusak testifies to his understanding of the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance, and that

Applicants—including their routing consultants Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. (“Kimley-

Horn”) and Half Associates, Inc. (“Halff”)—evaluated property boundaries, existing compatible

corridors, and locations of existing developments and habitable structures in order to route in a

manner that reasonably avoided population centers and other locations where gatherings are held. 5

Mr. Marusak explained that the Commission’s policy “does not mean that a proposed transmission

line must avoid habitable structures at all costs, but that reasonable alternatives should be

considered.” 6 The Anderson Intervenors may disagree with Mr. Marusak’s conclusion, and they

are entitled to rebut his testimony or argue over the credibility of his opinion in briefing, but it’s

unquestionable that Mr. Marusak’s conclusion is founded on well-reasoned analysis that is fully

disclosed in his testimony and in Applicants’ Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route

Analysis (“EAARA”), which Mr. Marusak sponsors and helped prepare.

2. Marusak Direct at 9:22-10:2

        The Anderson Intervenors object to the following statement they assert is in Mr. Marusak’s

direct testimony: “the routing process ‘identif[ied] areas where constraints are absent or fewer.’” 7


4
  Anderson Intervenors’ Objections at 2.
5
  The Direct Testimony of Russell Marusak (“Marusak Dir.”) at 20:20-21:17 (Mar. 26, 2026) (Item No. 77).
6
  Id. at 21:5-7.
7
  Anderson Intervenors’ Objections at 2.

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                       3
 The objections assert that Mr. Marusak’s statement is “unsupported as applied to Link M8.”8

Notably, the Anderson Intervenors objections mischaracterize Mr. Marusak’s testimony only to

fabricate an objection to it. A review of his testimony confirms that Mr. Marusak generally

describes Halff and Kimley-Horn’s constraints identification process and asserts only that the

“goal of this approach is to identify areas where constraints are absent or fewer…” 9 The statement

made no claim about particular routes or links, and notably made no mention of Link M8. Rather,

his testimony discusses the intention of the data collection process. And as the consultant

performing the data collection process, Mr. Marusak can undoubtedly testify to the goals of same.

The Anderson Intervenors stated no legitimate basis to find Mr. Marusak’s testimony is

unsupported.

3. Marusak Direct at 17:18-22

        The Anderson Intervenors object to Mr. Marusak’s direct testimony where he states that

Halff and Kimley-Horn “considered modifications to preliminary alternative route links, removal

of preliminary route links, and the addition of new alternative route links” and where Mr. Marusak

testifies that the public involvement program satisfied the requirements of 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4). 10

The Anderson Intervenors state no basis for their objection—they simply write “Objection.” 11 The

objection argues about the adequacy of Applicants’ public meeting under 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4),

and states that Mr. Marusak’s testimony concluding that the public involvement process was

adequate is “misleading as applied to the landowners affected by Link M8.” 12




8
  Id.
9
  Marusak Dir. at 9:22-10:1 (emphasis added).
10
   Anderson Intervenors’ Objections at 3.
11
   Id.
12

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                 4
          The Anderson Intervenors mischaracterize Mr. Marusak’s testimony. Mr. Marusak never

concludes that the public meeting process complied with 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4). Instead, Mr.

Marusak’s testimony provides a factual recount all of the actions performed by Applicants, Halff,

and Kimley-Horn in hosting the public meetings.13 As a result, the Anderson Intervenors cite no

line in Mr. Marusak’s testimony where he actually concludes compliance with 16 TAC §

22.52(a)(4) because no such line exists. Mr. Marusak’s testimony is merely factual, explaining that

after the public meeting, link adjustments were considered and made. None of these facts can be

disputed by the Anderson Intervenors and they are certainly not objectionable. To the extent that

the Anderson Intervenors disagree with the adequacy of Applicants’ public meeting, that is an

issue to be raised in intervenor direct testimony or in briefing, but there is no basis to object to the

factual statements in Mr. Marusak’s testimony about the public participation process.

4. Marusak Direct at 21:21-22:2

         The Anderson Intervenors object to Mr. Marusak’s testimony providing that

“[c]onstruction of the Proposed Transmission Line Project should not have significant impact on

existing . . . cultural resources.” 14 The Anderson Intervenors again object to Mr. Marusak’s

testimony, arguing that it is conclusory as applied to M8.15 Mr. Marusak’s conclusion that the

project should not have a significant impact on existing cultural resources is supported by the

several-hundred page EAARA that Mr. Marusak helped prepare. 16 Whether the Anderson

 Intervenors agree with Mr. Marusak’s conclusion is irrelevant to the admissibility of Mr.

Marusak’s well-supported statements. The objection should be overruled.

B. Objections to the testimony of Casey Petty

1. Petty Direct at 16:3-4

        The Anderson Intervenors object to the direct testimony of Casey Petty where she

concludes that all 122 filed routes comply with the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.17

The Anderson Intervenors argue, again, that this statement is unsupported “[t]o the extent any filed

route includes Link M8.” 18 The Anderson Intervenors disagree with Ms. Petty’s conclusion on

prudent avoidance and, in arguing her testimony is unsupported, recite a laundry list of routing

criteria that have nothing to do with prudent avoidance such as stream crossings, riparian crossings,

highway paralleling, and others. 19 The Anderson Intervenors fail to explain how Ms. Petty’s

statement is conclusory. Ms. Petty’s statement is based on the analysis she performed in selecting

the 122 filed routes, which she details extensively in her 76-page routing memorandum attached

as Exhibit CDP-6 to her direct testimony. 20 The Anderson Intervenors’ objection should be

overruled because Ms. Petty’s testimony is adequately supported and her well-reasoned

justification for her statement is disclosed in her testimony and testimony exhibits.

C. Objections to the testimony of Corin E. Cooley, P.E.

1. Cooley Direct at 20:14-21

        Ms. Cooley’s direct testimony provides that, “Based on the information available at this

time, the study area does not contain any known engineering constraints that cannot be resolved

 with additional consideration during the design and construction phases” and acknowledges that

“the Applicants have not performed on-the-ground geotechnical or subsurface surveys on private

properties.” 21 The Anderson Intervenors assert no basis for their objection to Ms. Cooley’s

testimony—they only write “Objection.”

        The Anderson Intervenors admit that “FEMA has not yet completed modern flood hazard

mapping for Menard County…” but argue that Applicants should nevertheless have provided

specific direct testimony addressing the structural integrity of their towers in these catastrophic

flood zones. 22 Applicants imply that Ms. Cooley should have provided a detailed discussion of

every conceivable constraint in the study area in support of her statement. Such a standard is

untenable and unnecessary. That the Anderson Intervenors identified a specific constraint that they

feel should have been addressed specifically in Ms. Cooley’s testimony does not disprove the truth

of Ms. Cooley’s testimony or mean it is unsupported.

2. Cooley Direct at 16:9-12

        The Anderson Intervenors object to Ms. Cooley’s testimony which provides, “In

consultation with LCRA TSC, I estimate the transmission line costs for the Proposed Transmission

Line Project to range from approximately $1,636,232,000 to $1,857,768,000, depending on the

route selected by the Commission.” 23 Again, the Anderson Intervenors fail to state what their

objection to this testimony is. Instead, they complain that Applicants’ cost estimates “lack per-link

granularity” and they cannot “assess the incremental cost of Link M8 as compared to alternative

links in the same corridor.” 24 However, the format in which Applicants provided their cost

 estimates does not impact the veracity of Ms. Cooley’s testimony, is not a valid basis for an

objection. The objection should be overruled.

D. Objections to the testimony of Kelly Wells

1. Wells Direct at 16:6-10

        Ms. Wells’ testimony provides, “LCRA TSC and Oncor have followed applicable

regulatory requirements, including notice requirements.” 25 Again, the Anderson Intervenors

dispute Applicants’ compliance with the public participation process and assert an undefined

objection to Ms. Wells’ testimony. They state no legitimate basis that the statement in Ms. Well’s

testimony is objectionable. Therefore, the objection should be overruled.

2. Wells Direct at 15:16-18

        The Anderson Intervenors assert an unspecified “objection” to Ms. Well’s testimony that

LCRA TSC “supports all 122 routes in the Application, and any reasonably forward-progressing

route that can be delineated from the 171 individual route segments as viable options.” 26 The

Anderson Intervenors argue that Ms. Wells’ statement “should be given no weight” because the

“Commission’s task is to evaluate and compare links, not to ratify a blanket endorsement.” 27 This

is not a proper objection and should be overruled. As a representative for LCRA TSC, Ms. Wells

is certainly entitled to testify to LCRA TSC’s support of all 122 routes and 171 individual route

segments.

3. Wells Direct at 14:18-20




25
   Direct Testimony of Kelly Wells (Wells Dir.) at 16:6-7 (Mar. 26, 2026) (Item No. 79).
26
   Anderson Intervenors’ Objections at 6.
27
   Id.

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                         8
         Ms. Wells’ testimony asserts that the filed routes “utilize compatible routing corridors by

paralleling existing ROW, property lines, and other natural or cultural features.” 28 The Anderson

Intervenors assert an unspecified “objection” to her testimony, arguing that Ms. Wells should have

“explain[ed] why Link M8’s heavy reliance on highway paralleling, rather than paralleling existing

electric facilities, is consistent with the structure of the Commission’s rule.” 29 It is unclear what

the Anderson Intervenors find objectionable about Ms. Wells’ statement, but it appears as though

they simply have questions about why Link M8 follows its chosen alignment. This is not a valid

basis for an objection, and Ms. Wells’ testimony appropriately and correctly states that the filed

routes utilize compatible routing corridors, which the Anderson Intervenors admit in their

objections.

E. Objections to the testimony of Jared Gurley

1. General Objection to Gurley Testimony

        The Anderson Intervenors seemingly assert an unspecified, general objection to the

testimony of Jared Gurley “to the extent Gurley’s testimony is offered or cited to justify the

selection of Link M8 over alternative links in the Menard County corridor.” 30 There is no basis

provided for the objection and no specific testimony is cited. The Anderson Intervenors continue

to assert invalid objections to testimony that should be the subject of intervenor direct testimony

or cross examination of Applicants’ witnesses at the hearing on the merits rather than objections.

For these reasons, the objection should be overruled.

F. General Objections



28
   Wells Dir. at 14:18-20.
29
   Anderson Intervenors’ Objections at 7.
30
   Id.

Applicants’ Response to the
Anderson Intervenors’ Objections                  9
 1. Lack of Specific Route Inquiry

        The Anderson Intervenors’ objection to any testimony or exhibit that asserts that all 171

link segments are equally compliant with PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101 should be

overruled. While some routes perform better than others with respect to discrete routing criteria,

all Applicants’ routes and route segments do equally comply with the statute and Commission

rules. The Anderson Intervenors’ fail to articulate a specific objection that is capable of being

sustained, but they are entitled to evaluate the routes based on the criteria laid out in PURA and

Commission rules in their testimony or briefs.

2. Evidentiary Objections

        The Anderson Intervenors generally “object to any testimony or exhibit to the extent it is

offered without proper foundation, is speculative, constitutes an improper legal conclusion, or is

outside the scope of the witness’s expertise.” 31 They fail to assert specific objections to testimony

or exhibits that are redressable by the ALJs. “Evidentiary objections must be timely, specific, and

afford the trial court an opportunity to cure the alleged error, if any. The Texas Rules of Evidence

require the ALJs to rule on the specific admissibility of individual testimony and exhibit as they

are offered, not in sweeping classifications.” 32

                                         III.     CONCLUSION

        For the foregoing reasons, the Anderson Intervenors’ Objections to Applicants’ direct

testimony should be overruled in their entirety. The objections are untimely, having been filed
